newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes edge higher, boosted by Iraq and stats.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes edge higher, boosted by Iraq and stats.

text.p: U.S. crudes were stronger Tuesday in a choppy session dominated again by shortcovering on concerns the confrontation between Iraq and the United States may not be completely settled.
Crude traders said the market was dull and lifeless. Refiners have taken to the sidelines until the wide price fluctuations run their course.
A Texas broker said the outright value of October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing remained too expensive based on the Middle East situation, ignoring weak margins and fundamentals.
Oct WTI/Cushing ended at $23.35-$23.45, 10 cts stronger.

Late Tuesday afternoon the market was bosltered by the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) stock report, notably in the distillates where stocks built only 235,000 barrels (bbls) for the week ended Sept 13.
Crude stocks were off 2.08 million bbls, gasoline stocks gained 434,000 bbls and runs were slightly higher at 95 pct.
Ahead of the statistics, outright crudes rose on Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz saying the increased U.S. military presence in the region was a prelude to new strikes.
In the cash domestic grade market, only a few deals were seen, and those trades were consumated at steady price levels.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was sold last at 27cts and 28 cts over WTI/Cushing, steady with Monday. Midland/WTI was heard traded at 7 cts over the WTI, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire talked either side of unchanged.
Sour grades were qiet in the afternoon. Last trades for West Texas Sour/Midland remained at minus $1.17-$1.19 to the WTI/Cushing.
Eugene Island was done Tuesday at slightly weaker values, both in the morning at a discount of $1.14 to WTI, and later in the session at minus $1.17 to the benchmark.
Oct Postings Plus was sold weaker in line with the Oct/Nov spread moves. Last deals were seen at $2.05 and $2.07, after trading earlier in the market at $2.12 amd as high as $2.15.
In the Brent aftermarket, partial deals were seen for Nov Brent at $21.69 a barrel, 4 cts weaker than the IPE close at $21.73.
Spreads firmed in the U.S. Brent session, trading in the aftermarket at plus 58 cts for Dec/Jan frame.
